purpose: V4 expansion batch: NEW whole-experiment directional A/B cases authored under strict blinding discipline (neutral, parallel, mechanic-only control/treatment strings; no valence; no outcome leak). Each scored case has its real winner VERIFIED from a primary/credible source before locking. Mirrors the PORTFOLIO_CASES_V3 scored-set schema field-for-field so the existing portfolio harness can load it. real_winner/effect/counter_intuitive/etc are GROUND-TRUTH fields only and are never rendered into the blinded stimulus.

methodology.blinding_discipline: Both arms describe only the MECHANIC of each change, factually, in parallel structure, with symmetric detail and tone. No evaluative adjectives ('improved', 'streamlined', 'more appealing'), no outcome numbers, no 'winner of N', no hint of which arm won. A blind reader must not be able to infer the winner from valence. real_winner/effect live ONLY in ground-truth fields.
methodology.verification: Each scored winner was confirmed against a primary source (peer-reviewed paper abstract/full-text or first-party operator report) by an independent web-research pass before locking. Cases whose claimed winner could NOT be verified against the primary source, or that contradict it, are NOT included in scored_cases — they are moved to held_back with verify:false and a note, per the no-fabrication rule.
methodology.scoring: direction_accuracy (did the sim pick the real winner?) is the headline; magnitude is out of scope for narrative/vendor cases. Run each case through the real agent-simulation engine on the rendered, BLINDED stimulus — never ask an LLM 'which wins?' directly (that measures memorization).
methodology.latent_winner_care: S4 (loyalty stretch goal) carries a LATENT-WINNER risk: net effect vs goal-attainment subgroup effects differ in sign. It is held_back here (see note) because the primary source contradicts the supplied winner. S5 is a NULL/backfire (control wins where a lift is expected) and is marked counter_intuitive accordingly.

scored_cases.control: The storefront places an outlet section in the main navigation, lets shoppers sort the catalog by size of discount, and marks reduced items with a '% off' badge.
scored_cases.treatment: The storefront organizes the main navigation by product category, sorts the catalog with full-price items first, and labels each item with its current list price.
scored_cases.metric: average selling price, gross margin, and conversion
scored_cases.effect: treatment > control; the version without discount-surfacing won on average selling price, gross margin, and conversion (institutional figures: ~+38% ASP, ~+35% margin, up to +23% conversion; >100k shoppers)
scored_cases.credibility: high (Ngwe, Ferreira & Teixeira, JMR 2019 56(6):944-959, field experiment); effect-size magnitudes from HBS institutional write-up (paywalled results tables); direction-only scoring
scored_cases.source: Ngwe, Ferreira & Teixeira, 'The Impact of Increasing Search Frictions on Online Shopping Behavior,' Journal of Marketing Research 2019 56(6):944-959, DOI 10.1177/0022243719865516
scored_cases.status: NEW v4 expansion 2026-06-17; winner verified from primary abstract + HBS institutional source

scored_cases.control: The gift certificate is valid for three weeks from issue.
scored_cases.treatment: The same gift certificate is valid for two months from issue.
scored_cases.effect: control > treatment; the three-week window had a higher redemption rate (~31% vs ~6%; 10/32 vs 2/32, n=64)
scored_cases.credibility: high (Shu & Gneezy, JMR 2010 47(5):933-944, randomized study); small n (64); magnitude from authors' institutional summary cross-checked arithmetically
scored_cases.source: Shu & Gneezy, 'Procrastination of Enjoyable Experiences,' Journal of Marketing Research 2010 47(5):933-944, DOI 10.1509/jmkr.47.5.933
scored_cases.status: NEW v4 expansion 2026-06-17; winner verified from primary abstract + UCLA Anderson institutional figures

scored_cases.control: The referrer earns a fixed reward of a stated point value for a successful referral.
scored_cases.treatment: The referrer earns a variable reward of the same expected value for a successful referral, awarded as a stated chance at a larger point value.
scored_cases.effect: treatment > control; the uncertain sender reward produced more referrals (+20.9%, coef 0.253)
scored_cases.credibility: high (Li, Belo & Li, Management Science 2024, field experiment, 160k+ users, 2x2 equal-expected-value design); DOI 10.1287/mnsc.2024.05685
scored_cases.source: Li, Belo & Li, 'Can Reward Uncertainty Encourage Social Referrals?', Management Science 2024, DOI 10.1287/mnsc.2024.05685
scored_cases.status: NEW v4 expansion 2026-06-17; winner + exact effect verified from authors' full-text manuscript. PAIRS with referral_reward_recipient_certainty (sign flips).

scored_cases.control: The referred friend earns a fixed reward of a stated point value when they accept a referral.
scored_cases.treatment: The referred friend earns a variable reward of the same expected value when they accept a referral, awarded as a stated chance at a larger point value.
scored_cases.effect: control > treatment; the uncertain recipient reward produced fewer referrals (-12.3%) — sign flips vs the sender-side variant
scored_cases.credibility: high (Li, Belo & Li, Management Science 2024, same field experiment as the sender variant); DOI 10.1287/mnsc.2024.05685
scored_cases.source: Li, Belo & Li, 'Can Reward Uncertainty Encourage Social Referrals?', Management Science 2024, DOI 10.1287/mnsc.2024.05685
scored_cases.status: NEW v4 expansion 2026-06-17; sign flip verified directly from abstract+results. PAIRS with referral_reward_sender_certainty.

scored_cases.control: The promotion is shown with a countdown timer and a time-limited framing, alongside the price and offer terms.
scored_cases.treatment: The promotion is shown as a standing offer with an open-ended availability framing, alongside the identical price and offer terms.
scored_cases.effect: treatment > control online; the time-limited framing failed to lift online willingness-to-pay (null-to-backfire), while the no-urgency version did not lose; a retailer-exogenous justification for the time limit can restore the urgency effect
scored_cases.credibility: high source (Hmurovic, Lamberton & Goldsmith, JMR 2023 60(2):299-328); direction confirmed from abstract + AMA editorial summary; exact effect sizes not retrieved (paywalled); direction-only scoring
scored_cases.source: Hmurovic, Lamberton & Goldsmith, 'Examining the Efficacy of Time Scarcity Marketing Promotions in Online Retail,' Journal of Marketing Research 2023 60(2):299-328, DOI 10.1177/00222437221118856
scored_cases.status: NEW v4 expansion 2026-06-17; NULL/backfire case (control-side wins where a lift is expected). Winner verified from primary abstract.

scored_cases.control: Hovering over a product image magnifies the region under the cursor.
scored_cases.treatment: Product images are presented at a single fixed display size.
scored_cases.effect: treatment > control; the page without hover-zoom had a higher purchase likelihood (abstract: 'zoom is associated with a decreased purchase likelihood'); effect magnitude not published openly
scored_cases.credibility: high (Naegelein, Spann & Molitor, Decision Support Systems 2019 121:109-120, randomized field experiment); effect size paywalled; direction-only scoring
scored_cases.source: Naegelein, Spann & Molitor, 'The value of product presentation technologies on mobile vs. non-mobile devices,' Decision Support Systems 2019 121:109-120
scored_cases.status: NEW v4 expansion 2026-06-17; winner verified from primary abstract. NOTE: the paper's separate 'alternative photos' technology had the opposite sign (raised purchases); this case isolates HOVER-ZOOM only.

scored_cases.control: The homepage carousel rotates through 12 items.
scored_cases.treatment: The homepage carousel rotates through 16 items.
scored_cases.effect: treatment > control after SRM correction (+3.3% engagement); the uncorrected analysis appeared negative because a sample-ratio mismatch — caused by bot-filtering removing the most-engaged treatment users — biased the treatment downward
scored_cases.credibility: high (Kohavi, Tang & Xu, Trustworthy Online Controlled Experiments 2020, SRM chapter; Fabijan et al., KDD 2019; Microsoft Research SRM article); SRM-corrected winner confirmed across primary/authoritative sources
scored_cases.source: Kohavi, Tang & Xu, Trustworthy Online Controlled Experiments (2020); Fabijan et al., 'Diagnosing Sample Ratio Mismatch in Online Controlled Experiments,' KDD 2019
scored_cases.status: NEW v4 expansion 2026-06-17; SRM-corrected winner = 16 items VERIFIED (naive result inverted by bot-filtering of heavy users). This was the flagged 'verify before locking' case; verified.

scored_cases.control: The donation banner reads '4 days left to donate.'
scored_cases.treatment: The donation banner reads 'Only 4 days left to donate.'
scored_cases.effect: treatment > control in the head-to-head; the 'Only' banner had higher dollars per impression (~$0.0076 vs ~$0.0067, ~+13%)
scored_cases.credibility: med (Wikimedia Meta first-party fundraising test log, 2010); direction from operator's own Banner-testing page; significance/raw counts for this specific late-December comparison not retrieved; direction-only scoring
scored_cases.source: Wikimedia Meta-Wiki, Fundraising 2010/Banner testing (Dec 28 2010 'Only vs. No Only' test)
scored_cases.status: NEW v4 expansion 2026-06-17; winner verified from first-party test log. NOTE: a different 'If everyone... donated $5' banner beat both 'days left' variants that season; this case scores the 'Only' vs no-'Only' matchup only.

scored_cases.control: The file-upload dropzone uses a thin border and a small upload button.
scored_cases.treatment: The file-upload dropzone uses a thick border and a large upload button.
scored_cases.effect: treatment > control by a small margin; upload completion 37.47% vs 36.18% (+3.58% relative)
scored_cases.credibility: med (Mozilla Firefox Test Pilot first-party blog; Firefox Send experiment); no formal significance test reported; small effect; direction-only scoring
scored_cases.source: Danny Coates, 'Kicking the tires on A/B testing,' Firefox Test Pilot (Medium), Oct 2 2017
scored_cases.status: NEW v4 expansion 2026-06-17; winner verified from first-party post. Small effect, not statistically certified by the team.

scored_cases.control: Each vendor listing shows the vendor's name and services.
scored_cases.treatment: Each vendor listing shows the vendor's name and services, plus a count of how many times the vendor has been viewed.
scored_cases.effect: treatment > control; showing the popularity count raised clicks on average (baseline DiD coef ~0.16-0.18, p<0.01), with a disproportionately larger gain for narrow-appeal vendors (interaction ~0.35-0.47, p<0.01) — broad-appeal vendors also gained, niche vendors gained more
scored_cases.credibility: high (Tucker & Zhang, Management Science 2011 57(5):828-842, field experiment); coefficients from authors' full-text PDF; DOI 10.1287/mnsc.1110.1312
scored_cases.source: Tucker & Zhang, 'How Does Popularity Information Affect Choices? A Field Experiment,' Management Science 2011 57(5):828-842, DOI 10.1287/mnsc.1110.1312
scored_cases.status: NEW v4 expansion 2026-06-17; winner verified from primary full-text. NOTE: niche vendors gain DISPROPORTIONATELY more (not exclusively); no winner-take-all flock to mainstream vendors.

held_back.control: The loyalty member receives a standard reward offer.
held_back.treatment: The loyalty member receives an offer that requires raising their nights a set percentage above their own prior baseline to earn a reward.
held_back.held_back_reason: PRIMARY SOURCE CONTRADICTS the supplied winner. Wang, Lewis, Cryder & Sprigg (Marketing Science 2016 35(4):565-575, n=95,532) report the published abstract verbatim: 'the promotion led to INCREASED purchasing in the post-promotion period' — i.e., the stretch-goal TREATMENT raised net post-period spend, so control did NOT win on net. The 'control wins / treatment lowers spend' story holds ONLY for the goal-FAILURE subgroup (80% who missed the goal); the 20% who hit it spent more, and the net treatment effect was positive. This is the LATENT-WINNER risk flagged in the brief: net vs subgroup effects differ in sign. Per the no-fabrication rule, NOT scored. If re-scoped to the goal-failure subgroup specifically, the control-side direction could hold, but the whole-experiment net winner is treatment — author with caution and re-verify in-text coefficients (paywalled) before any inclusion.
held_back.source: Wang, Lewis, Cryder & Sprigg, 'Enduring Effects of Goal Achievement and Failure Within Customer Loyalty Programs,' Marketing Science 2016 35(4):565-575, DOI 10.1287/mksc.2015.0966

held_back.control: A video ad plays before the content (pre-roll).
held_back.treatment: A video ad plays after the content (post-roll).
held_back.held_back_reason: COULD NOT VERIFY from the cited source. Kohavi et al. 2009 (Controlled Experiments on the Web, DMKD 18(1):140-181) contains NO pre-roll-vs-post-roll video-ad return-rate experiment (full text read directly: zero occurrences of pre-roll/post-roll/video-ad-ordering or a pre/post return-rate A/B). The paper's actual ad example is the MSN home-page extra-offers test (adding 3 offer slots -> CTR -0.38%, p=0.02, scrapped) — which is ALREADY in PORTFOLIO_CASES_V3 as 'msn_homepage_extra_offers'. The S7 claim appears to be a conflation/misattribution. No peer-reviewed controlled experiment found showing post-roll beats pre-roll on net return. Per the no-fabrication rule, NOT scored.
held_back.source: (claimed) Kohavi et al., DMCS/DMKD 2009 — verified to NOT contain this experiment

balance_check.note: This V4 batch skews treatment-won (8/10). Cases were selected for VALIDITY (verified primary source, blinding-clean, in-scope), NOT to engineer balance. Several 'treatment-won' cases are counter-intuitive in the same family the portfolio targets (friction wins, no-urgency wins on WTP, no-zoom wins, fixed-vs-uncertain reward sign flip). When merged into the full scored portfolio, recompute the always-treatment baseline so the combined headline dir_acc is held to the right floor. Two cases (S4 loyalty stretch goal, S7 pre/post-roll) were HELD BACK (verify:false), not scored.

held_out_memorization_note: Most cases here are obscure/peer-reviewed (low memorization risk). Highest memorization risk in this batch: donation_banner_only_word (Wikimedia 'Only' is a retold CRO anecdote) and apparel_hide_discount_surfacing (HBS-publicized 'frictions help' result). If the sim aces these but flunks the obscure peer-reviewed ones, suspect recitation.
